seeed_xiao_esp32s3_sense.name: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense

pads._comment: All 14 castellated pads, from the committed GLB's gold-pad islands (tools/pin_anchors.mjs, #e7c863): two rows of 7 at 2.54 mm pitch, USB-C at -X, +Y component side — so z=+1.76 is the D0–D6 edge and z=-13.98 the power/D10–D7 edge.

pinout.label: Chirp / buzzer
pinout.use: Passive piezo (LEDC PWM 2 kHz)

pinout.label: Status RGB LED
pinout.use: External WS2812 — pin defined but not driven by canary-wap firmware yet; the live indicator is the onboard LED (GPIO21).

pinout.label: Tamper
pinout.use: Reed / hall switch (INPUT_PULLUP, active-low) — FEATURE_TAMPER_GPIO defined but not yet consumed by canary-wap firmware.

pinout.label: VBAT sense
pinout.use: 2:1 divider, VBAT_DIVIDER_RATIO=2.0

pinout.label: GNSS UART
pinout.use: L76K TX/RX @ 9600 (FEATURE_GNSS)

pinout.label: Battery
pinout.use: JST-PH LiPo, charged by the onboard charger

pinout.label: Power
pinout.use: USB-C 5 V in; 3V3 rail out

seeed_xiao_esp32s3_sense.blurb: 21 x 17.8 mm. ESP32-S3, 8 MB flash / 8 MB PSRAM, onboard LiPo charger; the Sense expansion adds the OV camera + PDM mic on a stacked B2B board. The WAP build uses the plain-facing pins for chirp, tamper, LED and GNSS.
seeed_xiao_esp32s3_sense.provenance: Seeed Studio open-hardware CAD (STEP). Redistributed here as the board's source of truth for the local viewer; see boards/vendor/README.md. Verify Seeed's licence terms before external redistribution.

seeed_grove_vision_ai_v2.name: Seeed Grove Vision AI V2

pinout.label: Grove I2C
pinout.use: Result bus (labels/boxes, addr 0x62) on the 4-pin Grove port — GND · VCC · SDA(white) · SCL(yellow). Host GPIOs: DevKit-C3 4/5, XIAO-C3 6/7 (D4/D5), XIAO-S3 5/6 (D4/D5). The 4-pin Grove connector isn't discretely modeled in the vendor demo-stand STEP, so this row stays table-only.

pinout.label: Camera
pinout.use: OV5647 / OV-series camera ribbon into the wide flat FPC connector on the module's edge

pinout.label: USB-C (model port)
pinout.use: The module's own USB-C: load/preview the AI model in SenseCraft and update Himax firmware. Cannot see the ESP32 — that's the XIAO's port.

pinout.label: Power
pinout.use: 3V3 / 5 V from the Grove cable or the XIAO socket rail

seeed_grove_vision_ai_v2.blurb: Himax WiseEye2 HX6538 (Arm Cortex-M55 + Ethos-U55 NPU) that runs the vision model on-board and hands the host only labels + boxes over I2C (address 0x62) — no pixels cross the wire. A XIAO seats in the module's XIAO-footprint socket (I2C + UART, zero wiring) and runs canary-vision; the module's own USB-C is the model/SenseCraft port, the XIAO's USB-C is the firmware port. The OV5647 rides the CSI flex and is posed per-device by the models (it is not rigid to the board). The vendor demo stand + loose camera from the source assembly are stripped, leaving just the module.
seeed_grove_vision_ai_v2.provenance: Seeed Studio CAD (STEP) supplied with a printable stand + camera shroud + adapter and a posed OV5647 camera. The generator strips all of that so only the board remains: the loose camera drops by name (rpi cam), and the printed stand/mount drops by a Y-plane cut (drop_below_y) — merge_primitives fuses the stand's solids into unnamed material buckets, so a name match can't reach them, but the stand sits entirely below the board with a clean air gap. The OV5647 rides a flex and is posed per-device by the models, not welded to the board. Verify Seeed's licence terms before external redistribution.

seeed_round_display_xiao.name: Seeed Round Display for XIAO

pinout.label: Display
pinout.use: 240x240 round panel

pinout.label: Backlight
pinout.use: PWM-dimmable (night floor)

pinout.label: Touch
pinout.use: Single-touch

pinout.label: RTC
pinout.use: Timekeeping across reboots

pinout.label: Storage
pinout.use: Journal / assets

pinout.label: Battery
pinout.use: LiPo, onboard charger; verify polarity

seeed_round_display_xiao.blurb: Ø 43.0 mm PCB disc (the “39 mm” in marketing copy is the glass), 1.28-in GC9A01 (240x240) with CST816S touch, PCF8563 RTC, microSD and a LiPo charger; it seats a XIAO on its back socket. The backlight on D6/GPIO43 is PWM-dimmable — that is the bedside night floor.
seeed_round_display_xiao.provenance: Seeed Studio CAD (SolidWorks STEP export). This export did not carry per-solid colours through the tessellator, so materials are assigned by geometry (dark PCB + grey glass); the shape is the vendor's exact model. Verify Seeed's licence terms before external redistribution.

seeed_xiao_esp32s3.name: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3

pads._comment: Same 2x7 castellations as the Sense, but this vendor STEP sits in its own frame: USB-C at +X (x=13.8), +Y component side. Pad centres are render-verified against the committed mesh. Names follow the XIAO ESP32-S3 footprint the same way the Sense entry documents its own: D0 sits at the USB end (so the +X pad of each row), and — this being the identical board to the Sense — the D0–D6 edge is the one that lands on the Sense's D-row under the same component-up/USB-forward chirality, here the z=-14.4 edge. The z=+2.4 edge carries the 5V/GND/3V3/D10–D7 rail.

pinout.label: Display SPI
pinout.use: SCK / MISO / MOSI to the Round Display GC9A01 (through the socket)

pinout.label: Backlight
pinout.use: PWM-dimmable panel backlight (the bedside night floor)

pinout.label: Touch / RTC I2C
pinout.use: CST816S touch + PCF8563 RTC share the I2C bus

pinout.label: Chime
pinout.use: Passive piezo for the future severity-tiered chime — UNPOPULATED in v0.1 firmware.

pinout.label: Battery
pinout.use: JST-PH LiPo pads on the underside (not modeled as distinct gold in this STEP, so table-only)

pinout.label: Power
pinout.use: USB-C 5 V in; 3V3 rail out

seeed_xiao_esp32s3.blurb: 21 x 17.8 mm. The plain XIAO ESP32-S3 (ESP32-S3, 8 MB flash / 8 MB PSRAM, onboard LiPo charger) with no Sense expansion — the same 2x7 castellated footprint that seats in the Round Display's socket for the Watch Station. The Watch build (canary-display-watch) runs on this host; the display's SPI/backlight/touch/RTC/microSD all come through the socket.
seeed_xiao_esp32s3.provenance: Seeed Studio open-hardware CAD (STEP) for the plain XIAO ESP32-S3 — the same base module as the Sense, without the stacked camera/mic daughterboard. Redistributed here as the board's source of truth for the local viewer; see boards/vendor/README.md. Verify Seeed's licence terms before external redistribution.

quectel_l76k_gnss.name: L76K GNSS Module for XIAO

pads._comment: The carrier's 2x7 castellations land on the identical XIAO footprint the Sense uses — pin_anchors (#e7c863) puts every pad at the SAME raw-mm coordinate as the committed Sense map (z=+1.76 D-row, z=-13.98 power/D7 row, x -5.88..9.36 at 2.54 mm). So the names transfer verbatim from the Sense's verified map; a XIAO stacked here mates pin-for-pin.

pinout.label: UART
pinout.use: GNSS NMEA out (module TX, on the D7 pad → host RX) / config in (module RX, on the D6 pad → host TX)

pinout.label: PPS
pinout.use: One-pulse-per-second time strobe (optional) — not broken out to a confidently-identifiable pad in this STEP

pinout.label: Power
pinout.use: 3V3 from the host rail

pinout.label: Antenna
pinout.use: Ceramic GNSS patch — needs open sky

quectel_l76k_gnss.blurb: The L76K GNSS module (Quectel L76K receiver + ceramic patch antenna) on a XIAO-footprint carrier. In the WAP field build it talks to the XIAO over UART at 9600 baud: the module's TX crosses to the board's RX (D7) and its RX to the board's TX (D6). The patch antenna wants a clear view of the sky — that is why the WAP goes outdoors.
quectel_l76k_gnss.provenance: Seeed Studio open-hardware CAD (STEP) for the L76K GNSS Module for XIAO — a Quectel L76K receiver + ceramic patch antenna on a XIAO-footprint carrier. Redistributed here as the board's source of truth for the local viewer; see boards/vendor/README.md. Verify Seeed's licence terms before external redistribution.
